subject: Urgent: Hosted API p95/p99 regression — cross-region pathing suspected
messages:
From: Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@brightbeam.ai>
To: support@redwood.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:34 -0400
Subject: Re: spike alert — p95/p99 up since 08:45 UTC (us-east)

Hi team,

We've been seeing a sustained p95 / p99 latency bump for the Hosted API since ~08:45 UTC this morning for our US traffic. Request RTTs have jumped ~220ms at p95 and we're also seeing a small uptick in 5xx errors (rate ~0.8%). This is hitting our user-facing inference endpoints and affecting streaming sessions.

Quick details:
- Customer region: US-east (us-east-1)
- Ingest: 2027-06-29 08:45 UTC
- Impact: p50 unchanged, p95 +220ms, p99 +450ms, error rate from 0.1% -> 0.8%
- Sample request IDs: rb-1f8a4c, rb-1f8a7d, rb-1f8b00

We've opened a ticket (BrightBeam-INC-1185) on our side and can provide traces. Can you confirm whether there are any known infra changes or routing updates that could cause cross-region handoffs? This looks like some requests for US customers are being routed to EU nodes.

We need ETA on a mitigation — this is impacting our SLA obligations.

Thanks,
Ethan

--
Ethan Lowe
SRE Lead, BrightBeam

Folks —

Tagging ops and SRE. BrightBeam is reporting a p95/p99 jump and possible US->EU handoff. Please triage immediately and loop me back with root cause hypothesis and short mitigation plan. Marissa, please stand ready to coordinate comms and credit requests with the customer.

Vivek

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:03:51 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: spike alert — p95/p99 up since 08:45 UTC (us-east)

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Confirmed increased RTTs on traces from BrightBeam sample IDs. Attached: p95-samples-29jun.csv and packet-trace-ny-to-eu.pcap.
- Observed that a subset (~7%) of requests originating from us-east ingress were being routed to the eu-west serving cluster due to an egress-map mismatch in the regional routing table. The mapping for the us-east prefix to primary egress changed at 07:59 UTC because of an automated peering failover triggered by transient congestion earlier this morning. The failover applied a fallback egress that prefers an older EU peering path for a narrow set of prefixes.
- Impact: additional cross-region RTT (+~180–240ms) and increased tokenization memory churn causing intermittent 5xxs under high concurrency.

Immediate mitigation in progress:
1) Reverted the peering fallback for affected prefixes (roll-back snap at 10:15 UTC).
2) Forced local egress pinning for BrightBeam's account to us-east for the next 3 hours while we monitor.
3) Captured packet-level traces and a sampling of application-level logs (see attachments).

Next steps:
- Complete full routing table reconciliation and push a fix to the automated failover rules to exclude customer prefixes tied to dedicated edge policies.
- Prepare customer-facing RCA and propose a one-time SLA credit for the 3-hour window.

I'll update in 30–45 mins with monitoring windows.

- Aditya

--
Aditya Rao
SRE, Serving Infrastructure
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:48:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: spike alert — p95/p99 up since 08:45 UTC (us-east)

Status update:
- Roll-back completed at 10:15 UTC; metric windows show p95 trending back toward baseline within ~20 minutes for the majority of traffic.
- For BrightBeam-tagged traffic we applied temporary egress pin at 10:22 UTC; p95 for their sample traces returned to pre-incident within 12–18 minutes.
- No code deploys required. Change was config-only; small risk window during the rollback (routing table apply takes ~60s per region) but we used staged apply and observed no additional errors.

Proposed durable fix:
- Modify automated peering failover rules to: a) exclude customer-dedicated prefixes and b) add health-check gating at control-plane level (not just dataplane observable).
- Create an alert in Console that surfaces when egress-map selection deviates from expected region for a customer tag.

Risk/ask: needs product sign-off to change failover policy. Will file a PR for review.

-Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Ops Lead, Network Reliability
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Executive Leadership <leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 13:02:09 -07:00
Subject: Executive summary: BrightBeam hosted API latency regression (US->EU pathing)

Leadership — summary and ask: quick synopsis below and recommended actions.

What happened:
- Automated peering failover (triggered 07:59 UTC) applied a fallback egress mapping that incorrectly preferred an EU path for a small set of us-east prefixes. This caused cross-region handoffs for a subset of Hosted API requests, increasing p95/p99 by ~180–240ms and briefly raising 5xxs to ~0.8% for some customers (notably BrightBeam).

Impact:
- Customer impact window: ~07:59 UTC -> 10:22 UTC (BrightBeam saw ~2.5 hours of elevated tail latency for some requests).
- Customer-visible degraded QoS; we have a BrightBeam support ticket and they requested confirmation and remediation.

What we did:
- SRE rolled back the faulty egress mapping (10:15 UTC) and applied an account-level egress pin for BrightBeam (10:22 UTC) — metrics returned to baseline within ~20 minutes for pinned traffic.
- Collected packet traces and application logs; relevant artifacts attached.

Root cause hypothesis:
- Control-plane rule intended to prefer local peering on failover was bypassed by an older fallback ruleet that referenced deprecated prefix sets. The automated failover logic lacked a gating rule for customer-dedicated prefixes.

Recommended actions (ask to leadership):
1) Approve a one-time SLA credit for BrightBeam for the incident window. Suggested: 10% of June hosted-API invoice (to be finalized by finance).
2) Approve immediate product change to the peering failover policy (exclude customer-dedicated prefixes). Product to review PR and push to canary within 48 hours.
3) Approve Console alerting enhancement to surface egress deviations (low-cost observability tweak).

Customer comms: Marissa, please draft an apology + summary + mitigation + timeline for RCA. Suggest we offer an expedited RCA and post-mortem call this week.

Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@brightbeam.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 17:04:09 -04:00
Subject: Re: Executive summary: BrightBeam hosted API latency regression (US->EU pathing)

Thanks for the quick triage and the pinning workaround — our telemetry shows the tail has returned to normal for US sessions. Appreciated the transparency and the packet traces were helpful for our audit.

We'd like a formal RCA and a short post-mortem call (30 mins) with the ops leads and Marissa this week. We'll also want written confirmation of the failover policy change before the fix is deployed.

A one-time credit sounds reasonable — Marissa, can you send details and an invoice offset once you have the suggested amount?

Thanks,
Ethan

--
